items.t: Popkum is a small unincorporated community in the Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) Electoral Area D, east of the City of Chilliwack, near Rosedale and Bridal Falls; the FVRD is the local government for its electoral areas, providing planning and development approvals, building inspection and bylaw enforcement among its electoral-area services, while member municipalities govern themselves — so City of Chilliwack zoning does not apply in Popkum.
The school on the Rosedale/Popkum/Bridal Falls side of the district is Rosedale Traditional Community School, 50850 Yale Rd, Rosedale.

Parks and services: Cheam Lake Wetlands Regional Park (FVRD) is a 107-hectare park of lake, marsh and forest in Electoral Area D at 53480 Elgey Road, Rosedale, where 184 different bird species have been recorded and pets and other domestic animals are not permitted, in accordance with FVRD Bylaw No. 1500, 2018. Health care: Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Road, Chilliwack, is the Fraser Health community hospital serving Chilliwack and nearby areas, providing 24/7 emergency and acute care.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Popkum

items.t: Chilliwack's OCP and zoning bylaw numbers do not apply in Popkum.

Manufactured-home pad rent (MHPTA), for the park product nearby: pad rent may rise at most once every 12 months, on 3 full months' notice, by no more than the yearly limit plus a proportional amount — 2026 = 2.3% plus proportional, 2027 = 2.2% plus proportional. That regime applies to pad tenancies like Mt Cheam's.

blocks.text: Good to know about Popkum condos

items.t: Chilliwack's rules are the wrong rules here, three times over. Popkum owners plan and build under the FVRD (not City of Chilliwack zoning), pay under the rural Taxation (Rural Area) Act regime — 5% after July 2 and a further 5% after October 31. A closing adjustment, zoning opinion or pricing sheet built on Chilliwack sources misstates this community on all three points.

A live development proposal is not stock — and its revised form dropped townhomes. An FVRD public notice for a Popkum major OCP amendment proposal records a March 10, 2026 public information meeting at Rosedale Traditional Community School and states the applicant's revised proposal removed all multi-family residential uses (townhomes and row homes), leaving single-family lots, secondary suites and commercial outdoor storage in the revised form described. A proposal under consideration creates no condos or townhomes to buy, and nothing from it is counted in. Popkum - Major OCP Amendment - 2026.pdf

At Mt Cheam Mobile Home Park, 52604 Yale Road, Rosedale, you buy a home and rent the pad (MHPTA governs, increases capped at 2.3% plus proportional for 2026 and 2.2% plus proportional for 2027, all-ages); at 53480 Bridal Falls Road you buy freehold strata land (no pad rent, SPA governs). Neither is in Popkum itself, both surface under Popkum / East Chilliwack searches, and the financing, resale and document packages are entirely different.

Cheam Lake is the area's park anchor — and pets are not permitted in it. Cheam Lake Wetlands Regional Park (107 hectares, 53480 Elgey Road, Rosedale; 184 bird species recorded) prohibits pets and other domestic animals under FVRD Bylaw No. 1500, 2018 — a practical point for a buyer choosing Popkum partly for dog-walking ground.

blocks.text: Popkum, the village under Mount Cheam

Popkum is the residential heart of FVRD Electoral Area D, the small rural district east of Chilliwack that it shares with Bridal Falls. The Province records Popkum as an official community on the south side of the Fraser River, and two reserves of the Popkum First Nation, Popkum 1 and Popkum 2, lie beside it. The village and the reserves are separate jurisdictions, so a property search here starts with confirming which side of that line a parcel sits on.

Local volunteers wrote the area’s history in a book called "In the Shadow of Mt. Cheam", which the FVRD now hosts in four parts: reminiscences, community stories, family stories and the 1985 homecoming. It is the best single read for anyone who wants to know how the farms and families of this stretch of the valley came to be.

Because Popkum is not a city, its services come from the FVRD, not from Chilliwack: Area D residents are served by FVRD community parks, fire protection, garbage collection, public transit, storm drainage, street lighting and water. The FVRD also posts a quarterly RCMP crime summary for Popkum on its Area D page, a quick way for a buyer to check the area before an offer.

Popkum’s homes come to market rarely: 4 houses closed here between November 2025 and October 2026, too few for a reliable typical price. A buyer looking here is usually choosing a quiet rural lot within a few minutes of Highway 1, and should expect to compare against Chilliwack and Agassiz sales to judge value.

Other regional districts' same-letter bylaws are a name collision, not citable. The process instead: confirm the parcel's plan designation and zone with the FVRD before relying on any use or building claim.

Property taxes — RURAL regime: Popkum is not in a city, town, district or village, so its properties are rural-area properties: the owner receives the tax notice from the Province's Surveyor of Taxes Office and pays the Province. No municipal flat penalty applies to this area.

blocks.text: Popkum: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Land use is governed by the FVRD, not City of Chilliwack bylaws, because Popkum is in Electoral Area D.
Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) land in the plan area is subject to Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) rules; check a specific parcel on the ALC map before assuming a non-farm use is allowed.
Small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH) rules allowing secondary suites province-wide also apply in regional district electoral areas, per the Province.

blocks.text: Popkum: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Pets are not permitted in Cheam Lake Wetlands Regional Park, a 107-hectare FVRD park with about 2 kilometres of trails and a floating boardwalk, because of its sensitive ecosystem.
Bridal Veil Falls Provincial Park is immediately east at the Highway 1 and Highway 9 junction, a day-use park centred on Bridal Veil Falls.
FVRD utility billing in Area D is quarterly, in January, April, July and October, unlike City of Chilliwack quarterly billing under city bylaws. Area D - Residential Rates 2026.pdf
No Fraser Valley Regional Library branch is in Popkum; the nearest branches listed are in Chilliwack and Agassiz — see the popkum note.

blocks.text: Popkum: costs and taxes

items.t: Popkum does not pay City of Chilliwack tax rates. In FVRD Area D, 2026 residential Water - Area D is metered at a $77.00 flat/minimum with $0.96 per cubic metre over 100 cubic metres, billed quarterly; Sewer - Area D and Drainage - West Popkum show no utility billing and are funded through taxation instead. Area D - Residential Rates 2026.pdf

The Speculation and Vacancy Tax (SVT) taxable-areas list names the City of Chilliwack, not FVRD Electoral Area D; check the provincial map for a specific Popkum parcel rather than assuming SVT applies.

Highway 1 access is at the Highway 9 interchange by Bridal Falls, east of Popkum, which is also the route north across the Fraser River toward Agassiz.
